group.passage:
During the COVID-19 pandemic, people are overwhelmed with terror and misleading information. Every day, a wealth of misleading information is published and widely spread on social media. Exposed to [[1]], people sometimes have difficulty differentiating between facts and myths.
The myth that the ingredients in COVID-19 vaccines are unsafe has previously proved incorrect, as the vaccines are mainly composed of ingredients which don’t pose a threat to human health. For example, Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna vaccines comprise Messenger RNA (mRNA) while the Novavax vaccine is made up of harmless spike protein from the virus that [[2]] COVID-19. To clarify the myth, some researchers have [[3]] the fact that mRNA doesn’t penetrate the nucleus of the cells, let alone modify human DNA. In fact, either mRNA or spike protein can activate immune responses by giving instructions to cells in the human body. Such a response can protect the body from contracting COVID-19. [[4]] the occurrence of immune responses, the body will instantly discard all the vaccine ingredients which are no longer needed.
To avoid falling for false information, people can verify the information by cross-checking it from different sources and credible websites. [[5]], people should report misleading information without hesitation and never share something unproven. With these feasible tips, people may avoid falling victim to false information.

tags.topic: debunking myths about COVID-19 vaccines and avoiding misinformation
